coverage: Four targeted cards; operation coverage is checked for this pilot, not claimed complete for the language.

ranges.text:
Buffer operations are pure. Signatures:
Bytes::empty()->Bytes
Bytes::length(Bytes)->I64
Bytes::at(Bytes,I64)->I64
Bytes::slice(Bytes,I64,I64)->Bytes
Bytes::push(Bytes,I64)->Bytes
Bytes::concat(Bytes,Bytes)->Bytes
Bytes::from_list(List<I64>)->Bytes
Text::bytes(Text)->Bytes
Text::valid(Bytes)->Bool
Text::from_bytes(Bytes)->Text
Text::length(Text)->I64
Text::at(Text,I64)->I64
Text::slice(Text,I64,I64)->Text
Text::concat(Text,Text)->Text
Bytes index/count units are raw bytes; Text index/count units are Unicode scalars. slice arguments are start,count, not start,end. at returns I64. Buffers are immutable; concat/push return new values. Text::bytes gives UTF-8 bytes; no implicit Text/Bytes conversion. Byte bounds, byte values outside0..255, invalid slice ranges and invalid UTF-8 in from_bytes fault at runtime, not by static type rejection. Text::valid reports UTF-8 validity as Bool.

nominal.text: Records/variants have nominal identity: similar fields do not make types interchangeable. A record update Type {...base,field:value} needs the same nominal record and generic arguments as base; unmentioned fields are preserved. Generic constructors can infer arguments from fields/payloads or an identifying expected nominal type. With such an expected variant type, a payload-free case may be written Case or Case(). No global case-name search occurs. A bare case without an identifying expected type is unresolved. Generic FUNCTION calls infer from argument constraints, not their expected return type; use explicit specialization when no argument determines a parameter. Declaration boundary types remain explicit. Match handles every case with matching arm result types.

propagation.text: try operand is prefix propagation: exactly two payload cases Ok(T),Err(E) are required in operand and enclosing output; error types match exactly, no conversion. Ok yields its payload; Err exits only the enclosing FUNCTION, including from loops or branches. Callers continue with the returned result. Direct prefix try is forbidden in requires/ensures. A PURE helper may use try in its own body and be called by a contract. The identifier try is legal for functions/variables. try(value) and try (value) are ordinary function calls, not propagation; they require a callable named try. Runtime faults are not caught. Postconditions run on propagated errors too. No implicit resource cleanup is added.

contracts.text: requires and ensures expressions must be Bool and pure, regardless of the enclosing function action declaration. Calls to any function with a nonempty DECLARED action bound are forbidden in contracts, even if its body is currently pure or its call is in an unreachable/short-circuited branch. All functions, branches and generic bodies are statically checked, including unused ones. Static checking establishes types/actions, not truth of preconditions/postconditions, termination or absence of runtime faults. A well-typed false contract or unexecuted faulting expression can pass check. On invocation, preconditions run before the body; postconditions run after normal or propagated results. Short-circuiting skips unevaluated calls at runtime only.
